The clinical presentation centers on a child with mucocutaneous bleeding—recurrent nosebleeds, gingival bleeding, unexplained bruising, and petechiae—predominantly on acral sites (hands and feet). PFA-100 is exquisitely sensitive for both vWD and many platelet function defects; abnormal closure times on epinephrine (but not ADP) cartridge strongly favor vWD, whereas abnormal closure on both cartridges raises suspicion for platelet dysfunction. vWF:Ag and vWF:RCo are definitive for diagnosing and subtyping vWD, and Factor VIII activity helps distinguish vWD (where FVIII is usually concordantly low) from isolated platelet disorders (where FVIII is normal). No red flags for malignancy, autoimmunity, or severe inherited disease (e.g., no hemarthroses, no post-surgical/menorrhagia history, no family history of severe bleeding mentioned) are present — so escalation to bone marrow biopsy or genetic panels is premature.
